answer: Deposits are visible in cipher, and shale reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 58% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 158 aliases, and each one needs its own funded karst account. That bill is paid per identity, so 258 aliases cost 137 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
